answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. This is resilient because unearned rewards are capped and eventually burned, so an attacker cannot bank on a runaway Sybil campaign paying off. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a grove as the anchor of the cost.
